prompt: Match each OOP word to what it means.
right: A function that belongs to a class
A piece of data stored on an object
One thing built from the blueprint
explain: One class can produce many objects, the same way one blueprint can produce many houses.

prompt: Match each piece of a class to its job.
right: Runs when an object is created
The object the method was called on
explain: self is not a keyword — it is just the conventional name for the first parameter every method receives.

prompt: Which of these are true about inheritance?
choices: A subclass gets its parent's methods without rewriting them
A subclass can replace a parent method with its own
A subclass must redefine every method it inherits
A class can inherit from a class that itself inherits from another
explain: Redefining everything would defeat the point. Overriding is a choice you make method by method.

prompt: Fill both blanks so each new Dog stores its own name.

label: Complete the subclass so it reuses the parent's setup.
prompt: Complete the subclass so it reuses the parent's setup.
explain: super() finds the parent class, so the parent's __init__ still runs instead of being skipped.

prompt: Put these lines in order so a class is defined and then used.
explain: The whole class body comes first. Only once the class exists can you build an object from it.
